title: October 25, 1980: Hindi cinema's most literary lyricist died at 58 - mid-conversation, playing cards with friends.

sources.text: Janata Weekly - Sahir Ludhianvi: The Magician whose songs live on

caption:
October 25, 1980: Hindi cinema's most literary lyricist died at 58 - mid-conversation, playing cards with friends.

Born Abdul Hayee in Ludhiana in 1921, he wrote some of Hindi film's most enduring lyrics - "Kabhi Kabhie," "Tumsa Nahin Dekha," "Jo Waada Kiya Wo Nibhana Padega," "Aye Meri Zohra Jabeen" - across a career that reshaped what a film song could say.

Before Sahir, film lyrics rarely carried the social conscience of his verse - his songs questioned poverty, war and injustice as often as they sang of love. India honoured him with the Padma Shri in 1971, nine years before his death.

Sahir's lyrics travelled further than most policy ever does - decades on, his lines are still quoted, still sung, still shaping how India hears itself.
